transcript.text: Every so often when I use the hob the electrics in the house go off. Not every time, maybe once a week. It's an induction hob, Hisense I think.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. Because your Hisense induction hob is causing the house electrics to trip, this points to an electrical fault—most likely an earth leakage in the power module, coil, or wiring. For safety, please stop using the hob until it has been checked by a qualified electrician; repeated tripping is a protective response to a genuine hazard. To help the engineer (or for your own awareness), could you check if there's any spillage near the edges that might be causing tracking? Also, does the trip happen on a specific cooking zone or randomly?
Yes, there have been a couple of boil-overs recently. I don't think it's one particular zone, it's usually when two are on high. There was also a faint electrical smell once after it tripped.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. The boil-overs are very likely the cause: liquid can seep under the glass and create a path to earth, especially when two high-power zones draw significant current. The faint electrical smell suggests there is internal damage or overheating occurring. Because this involves an active earth fault and potential fire risk, you must stop using the hob immediately and leave it isolated (switched off at the consumer unit if possible). Do not attempt to dry it out and then use it again; the internal components may already be compromised. Please have a qualified electrician or appliance engineer inspect the wiring and power module before considering any further use.

candidates: Earth leakage in the induction power module or coil (high)
Mains wiring or connection fault at the hob (medium)
